summary: Full text of the 2017 JRSM Open meta-analysis (7 placebo-controlled trials, 575 adults, acetate or gluconate lozenges, 80-207 mg/day elemental zinc) shows colds 33% shorter (95% CI 21-45%), with no added benefit above 100 mg/day. It gets the one eligible context, inside the signed lozenge-only scope (Dr. Pham rejected bridging to picolinate or capsules). The symptom-level and IPD analyses re-use the same acetate trials and are recorded without separate credit. The applicability source list is narrowed to 28515951; its acetate/gluconate lozenge constraints stay.

applicability.studied_population: Adults with an acute common cold; early short-term treatment, not prevention
applicability.reason: Reviewed preparation, population and purpose scope remains independent of amount. Dose reports descriptive research-exposure correspondence; it does not create a positive adequacy benchmark or Safety determination.

identity.name: Zinc acetate lozenges; the legacy record key does not turn this into picolinate-capsule evidence.

population.description: Three randomized placebo-controlled zinc acetate lozenge trials in adults with natural colds (the acetate subset of 28515951).

study_contexts.study_design: Meta-analysis of symptom-specific durations in three zinc acetate lozenge trials (80-92 mg/day).

outcomes.name: Nasal discharge -34%, congestion -37%, scratchy throat -33%, hoarseness -43%, cough -46%, muscle ache -54%; sneezing and sore throat CIs crossed zero; no difference for headache or fever.

limitations: No picolinate, swallowed-capsule or generic preventive transfer.
Preserve acute study exposure versus chronic upper-limit safety distinction.
Returned decision: Reject identity bridge; date-restricted evidence hold. Publication-age-only exclusions were withdrawn and are not adopted.

identity.name: Zinc acetate or zinc gluconate lozenges, not picolinate capsules.

population.description: Seven placebo-controlled randomized trials, 575 participants with naturally acquired common colds (3 zinc acetate, 4 zinc gluconate lozenge trials).

study_contexts.study_design: Meta-analysis (inverse-variance random effects) of placebo-controlled zinc lozenge trials with >75 mg/day elemental zinc; main outcome common cold duration; salt and dose subgroups.

outcomes.name: Main outcome, common cold duration: 33% shorter (95% CI 21% to 45%) with zinc lozenges; acetate 40%, gluconate 28% (difference 12 points, 95% CI -12 to +36, not significant).
Dose: 80-92 mg/day trials 33% versus 192-207 mg/day trials 35% (difference 2 points, -29 to +32); no evidence that >100 mg/day adds benefit.

limitations: Participant totals are not additive across overlapping reviews.
Acute lozenge results do not establish routine-safe long-term exposure or other zinc delivery efficacy.
Returned decision: Reject identity bridge; date-restricted evidence hold. Publication-age-only exclusions were withdrawn and are not adopted.

Included-study PMID membership was extracted from the source Results included-study enumeration. These are source membership identifiers, not independent efficacy approvals or automatic trial replications. Exact table/citation mapping and unindexed citations are retained in the source receipt.

Credit is limited to early short-term treatment of acute colds with zinc acetate or gluconate lozenges; signed A123 rejects the identity bridge to picolinate or swallowed capsules, and the existing applicability form/dosage-form constraints enforce that. Date-only restriction withdrawn.

Included-study identity: 6 of 7 PMIDs re-matched to the source reference list this session (32287355 retained from the prior binding). 80-207 mg/day exceeds the chronic upper limit and is acute-use only; safety assessment stays separate.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: Trial-specific repeated lozenge dosing while awake during the cold; no single pooled schedule.
co_therapies: Local lozenge composition and released-ion conditions are preparation-specific.
dose.reported_regimen: Elemental zinc 80-207 mg/day as acetate or gluconate lozenges in two clusters (80-92 and 192-207 mg/day) during acute colds.

normalization.basis: A heterogeneous synthesis has no single assigned-arm dose. Descriptive regimens do not create an intake recommendation, equivalent preparation or efficacy threshold.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC5418896): Abstract; Methods (eligibility >75 mg/day); Results (included trials, dose range, salt and dose comparisons, Figure on dosage); reference list.

clinical_review.notes: No separate credit: individual-patient-data reanalysis of the same three zinc acetate trials already inside 28515951; full text not retrievable via API.

limitations: Abstract: IPD from 3 zinc acetate lozenge RCTs, 199 patients; colds 2.73 days (one-stage, 95% CI 1.8-3.3) or 2.94 days (two-stage) shorter versus about 7 days average; effect not modified by allergy, smoking, severity, age, sex or ethnicity. Overlapping trials, not independent replication.
